query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is intended to retain the favorable mechanical performance of the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy while reducing cost and preserving a useful strength–ductility balance. Existing FeNiCrMn research has focused mainly on corrosion rather than dynamic loading. Molecular-dynamics studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys have examined temperature, strain rate, cracking, voids, and compositional variation, demonstrating condition-dependent mechanical responses, but they do not establish how to improve FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading. Given the constraints of remaining Co-free, controlling cost, and retaining balanced strength and ductility, what single intervention could improve the dynamic mechanical performance of FeNiCrMn over a defined range of temperatures and strain rates? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, the causal mechanism, a predicted outcome relative to unmodified FeNiCrMn, its boundary conditions, supporting evidence from prior studies, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing short-range ordering (SRO) in the FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy will improve its dynamic mechanical performance over a defined range of temperatures and strain rates.
generation.conditions: Defined range of temperatures and strain rates
generation.mechanism: SRO development leads to the formation of FCC-preferred (FCCP), BCC-preferred (BCCP), and indifferent (IND) clusters, which withstand higher stresses and improve mechanical properties
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved dynamic mechanical performance, including increased strength, ductility, and strain rate sensitivity
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 77 K to 900 K, strain rate range: 10^(-7) s^(-1) to 10^6 s^(-1)
generation.uncertainty: The exact optimal composition and processing conditions for introducing SRO in FeNiCrMn are unknown

falsification_experiment.design: Uniaxial tensile testing and molecular dynamics simulations
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of SRO does not lead to improved dynamic mechanical performance, the hypothesis is falsified

Own digest: Paper card. Question: Is it possible to introduce short-range ordering (SRO) in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) to simultaneously enhance both ultimate strength and ductility, and what microstructures and mechanisms are required?. System: Equiatomic CoCuFeNiPd high-entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Hybrid Monte Carlo (MC) and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations: MC site-occupancy swaps at 300 K and 1200 K using the Metropolis criterion, interchanged with MD relaxations (100 MC swaps followed by up to 100 MD relaxations per iteration) to optimize SRO; DFT calculations performed to validate cohesive energies.. Test conditions: Uniaxial tensile deformation simulations at strain rates of 2 × 10^8 s^-1 and 2 × 10^7 s^-1, at temperatures of 300 K and 1200 K; initial sample size 8788 atoms with lattice constant 3.6 Å..
